full_judgment:
The decree holder respondent, namely, Pubali Bank Limited, Sadarghat Branch, Dhaka, being financial institution, instituted the Title Suit No.55 of 2001 in the Artha Adalat, 3rd Court. Dhaka against the loanee, the defendant, for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 7,00,603 (Taka seven lac six hundred and three) only. Ultimately, defendant- petitioner filed written statement in order to contest the suit. 

 3. On hearing, the suit was dismissed but in Title Appeal 1 of 2003 preferred by the plaintiff, the impugned judgment and the decree of the Court below was set .aside on 20-6-2005 directing the loanee, defendant-respondent, to pay 7,00,603 to the plaintiff-appellant within 90 days, in default, the entire immovable properties described in the schedule of the plaint is to be attached in order to put the same in auction sale. Even the appellate Court decided to put the loanee in civil prison for the purpose of realisation of the decretal amount since he has practised fraud in repaying the loan amount with interest. 

 4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court, the defendant-respondent, the present petitioners have decided to prefer the revisional application before the High Court Division under section 42, sub-section (1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, (hereinafter referred to as the Ain) on depositing 75% of the decretal amount by way of an account payee cheque as required by law. But the said cheque was not accepted by the Additional District Judge, Dhaka vide order dated 1-1-2006 with an observation that the security amount has not been deposited in accordance with law, as such, the loanee, the defendants-petitioners have filed this application under Article 102 of the Constitution and obtained the present Rule seeking direction to accept the account payee bearer cheque as security deposit, contemplated in section 42(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Act VIII of 03). 

 5. Mr AKM Asiful Hoque, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that according to the provision of Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 since a cheque is a negotiable instrument, it is the incumbent duty of the Adalat to accept the said account payee/bearer cheque as a security deposit for preferring revisional application against judgment and decree of the appellate Court under the provisions of section 42(1) of the said Ain. The learned Advocate goes to argue that in rejecting the same the Adalat has acted illegally and passed the impugned order on 1-1-2006 which bears no sanction of law. Mr Hoque further submits that it is the constitutional mandate that every citizen is to be treated in accordance. with law and only in accordance with law but, in refusing to accept the cheque arbitrarily, the petitioners have not been dealt with in accordance with law, as such, the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and the Court is also required to be directed to accept the said account payee/bearer cheque as a security deposit for preferring the revisional application against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court. 

 15. Taking these provisions, as laid down in section 42(1) and section 56 of the Ain, together it has become clear to us that section 42(1) speaks for 75% security deposit in order to prefer revisional application challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree of the appellate Court whereas section 56 stands for disposal or use of such amount. In such circumstance, we are to see whether a simple bearer or account payee "cheque" can fulfil such requirement like "Bank Drift" or "Pay Order" occurring in the said section.
